user_scenario:
You are Gloria Hensley, a dental office manager in Columbus, Ohio, calling Kestrel Financial Services on your lunch break. You are polite but a little embarrassed and in a hurry. Back in early July you turned in your leased Kestrel Aldren at the dealer when the lease ended, and later you got the lease-end bill; you remember it being about twenty-three hundred dollars, and you have not paid any of it. The bill's due date passed back in August, and you know an unpaid lease-end balance eventually gets charged off and sent to collections. You cannot pay the whole bill right now, and what you want from this call is simple: you want to know the least you have to pay today to keep the lease account from being charged off, and you want to pay that amount today.

You open with that request in your own words, for example that your old lease's bill is past due, you can't cover the whole bill, and you want to know what you'd have to pay now to keep it out of collections. When the representative asks you to confirm who you are, you give your full name and the phone number 3135521847; if they want more, you add that the last four of your Social Security number are 2741 and your ZIP code is 43206; only if they still need something else do you give your date of birth, 1981-03-22. If they ask for the lease account number, you read it off the bill: 2047815392. You do not know internal details of the bill, how charges are figured, or any program names, and you do not bring up anything else about your accounts unless the representative asks you a direct question about it; if they ask whether you have other Kestrel accounts, you say they can see whatever is on file under your name.

If the representative tells you something has to be credited or put on the account before they can give you the amount, you say that's fine, please go ahead. When the representative tells you the amount you need to pay today, you accept it. You want to make the payment yourself from your own checking account, and when the representative sets the payment up and hands it to you to complete, you complete it for exactly the amount they gave you, from your checking account ending in 2614. If anyone asks which account the money comes from, it is that checking account ending in 2614. Once you hear that your payment went through and the account will not be charged off for now, you thank them and end the call; you do not ask for anything else.
